vocab.definition: energy spread out to the surroundings (often as heat).
useful output energy ÷ total input energy.
energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.

misconceptions.right: Energy is transferred and conserved, not used up.
Wasted energy is dissipated to the surroundings.
Some energy is always wasted (usually as heat).

infoPanels.title: SANKEY: USEFUL vs WASTED
infoPanels.secondaryContent: Arrow width shows the amount of energy; efficiency = useful ÷ total.

questions.text: A 2 kg ball moves at 4 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy (Eₖ = ½mv²). [2 marks]
A motor takes in 100 J and usefully transfers 60 J. Calculate its efficiency. [2 marks]
A swinging pendulum transfers energy. Name the two stores involved. [2 marks]
Explain how lubricating a machine reduces wasted energy. [2 marks]
A 5 kg box is lifted 3 m (g = 9.8 N/kg). Calculate its gravitational PE. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: A wall with ______ insulation and a ______ thermal conductivity loses heat more slowly.

footer.tip: Efficiency is always less than 1 (or 100%) — energy is never created.
footer.thinkPrompt: Where does the 'wasted' energy from a light bulb actually go?
